requirements.lead_text: Demonstrate that you know how to respond to electrical emergencies by doing the following:
requirements.req_text: Demonstrate that you know how to respond to electrical emergencies by doing the following: (a) Explain how to turn off power for a particular circuit and the whole house in the event of an emergency. (b) Demonstrate how to rescue a person touching a live wire in the home. (c) Describe how to safely get out of a car in an accident if you suspect a utility wire is on the car. (d) Show how to render first aid to a person who is unconscious from an apparent electrical shock. (e) Show how to treat an electrical burn. (f) Explain what to do in the event of an electrical fire. (g) Explain what to do if caught out in the open during an electrical storm.

pamphlet_excerpts: Using the Recovery Position: Place a victim who is unconscious but who is breathing normally in a recovery position (p. 46).
Keeping the Airway Clear: This will prevent the person from choking on saliva, blood (from a bitten tongue), or vomit, and will help keep the airway open (p. 46).
Monitoring Victim Breathing: Continue to monitor the person's breathing until medical help arrives (p. 46).
Spinal Injury Precautions: However, do not move a person with suspected spinal injury unless it is absolutely necessary (p. 46).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Monitor Breathing Continuously: Continue to monitor the person's breathing until medical help arrives (p. 46).
Step 2 - Protect Suspected Spinal Injuries: However, do not move a person with suspected spinal injury unless it is absolutely necessary (p. 46).
Step 3 - Position Victim Carefully: Recovery position for a person who may have a spinal injury (p. 46).
Step 4 - Locate Main Power Feeds: Electric current comes into your home on overhead or underground wires (p. 46).
